poBestPractice: Before submitting any PO request, carefully review the signature authorisation flow.
Submitting a PO request without checking the signature authorisation flow.
Submit the PO request at least two weeks before the scheduled start date.
Submitting at the last minute and leaving insufficient time for approval.
Ensure the Purchase Order is officially issued before any work begins.
Allowing work to start before the Purchase Order is issued.
Check VAT exemption or tax rules before PO submission.
Assuming the supplier is always tax exempt without checking.
Confirm both parties have signed the Contract before engagement.
Proceeding without a fully signed Contract.
Return the counter-signed Agreement to the supplier before start.
Failing to return the signed Agreement and leaving the supplier uninformed.
Verify the supplier’s framework contract is current.
Using a supplier whose framework contract deadline has expired.
Ensure the scope of work matches the terms of the Purchase Order.
Assigning work outside the agreed scope of the Purchase Order.
Check supplier registration and updated bank details before submission.
Submitting a PO for an unregistered supplier or with outdated bank details.
Maintain the Threshold Tracking Table when there is a new PO.
Neglecting to update cumulative threshold tracking.
Include a Work Plan with clear deadlines and deliverables.
Using vague or incomplete Work Plans.
Confirm the financial proposal precisely matches the scope of work.
Attaching a financial proposal that does not align with technical requirements.
Use only the most recent official templates.
Working with modified or outdated forms.
Reference scope, deliverables and details in every Purchase Order.
Leaving Purchase Orders disconnected from the work context.
Create separate Purchase Orders for unrelated activities.
Combining multiple unrelated services under a single Purchase Order.
Check that the PMM project and/or activity ID exists before requesting a PO.
Requesting a PO for an activity that is not recorded in the PMM IT tool.
Request the creation of a new supplier in FIMS through the Multiservice Assistant before submitting the file.
Submitting a PO file for a supplier that does not yet exist in FIMS.
Sign and date the contract after the PO is created and before the service delivery starts.
Signing a contract before the PO exists or after the work has already started.
Allow a longer period between consulting companies and the date of the event for which services are ordered.
Consulting event organisers so late that competition and quality suffer.
Follow the legal advice when it recommends not splitting a call for tenders.
Splitting a need into several smaller procedures against legal advice.
Define the form of deliverables clearly in consultant contracts and require documents, or at least a summary, in English or French.
Leaving deliverables vague or accepting outputs that cannot be read in an official language.
Define reduced-fee sanctions for delays or poor quality in the contract and have both parties accept them.
Having no agreed basis to reduce a fee when work is late or of low quality.
For restricted consultations, have the eligibility criteria assessed by at least two authorised secretariat members.
Letting a single staff member assess eligibility alone.
Review and update contract templates, with special attention to clauses that protect the Council's finances and rights.
Reusing old templates without checking their protective clauses.

paySteps.text: Confirm that the goods, services or deliverables covered by the PO/contract have actually been completed or received.
list: Obtain evidence of completion or delivery.
Confirm the relevant period/deliverable matches the contractual file.
Do not move to payment on an unaccepted output.
Certify the work with a Certificate of Acceptance of Work for consultants, or a Payment Request Memorandum for other types of expenditure.
The certificate is signed by the staff member who attended the event or received the goods or services.

paySteps.text: Match the payment to the PO, Order Form/AoE/Call-off and any amendments already approved.
list: Check supplier and contractual reference.
Confirm the payment relates to the approved scope.
Include amendments where applicable.

paySteps.text: Check the invoice against the supplier, agreed financial terms and the approved contractual package.
list: Verify invoice amount and currency.
Check invoice reference and supplier identity.
Resolve discrepancies before submission.

paySteps.text: Where the service type requires a final budget or evidence of financial changes, confirm these are complete and approved.
list: Use the final budget where required.
For event files, retain evidence of significant financial changes and CCM approval.
Keep exchange-rate evidence where required.

paySteps.text: Assemble the supporting evidence required for the selected service type.
list: Examples include consultant deliverables, event supporting documents, translated documents, work plans or proof of completed works.
Use the exact package shown in the Payment File Builder.
For events, include a signed list of participants confirming attendance, with a separate list for each day of a multi-day event.
Where the event format has no registration, use another form of evidence, such as a group photo of the participants.
Where a volume is difficult to confirm, attach at least a signed memo to the invoice showing how the amount was calculated from actual data.
For oral presentations by consultants, keep a record or documentation of the deliverable as evidence.

paySteps.text: Prepare the Payment Request and ensure the payment package is internally consistent.
list: Use the current official template.
Reference the correct PO/contract.
Check the supporting documents before signature/visa.
Complete the activity report (synopsis) in the PMM IT tool.

paySteps.text: Continue the visa/signature route already applied to the PO for the same service/expenditure type.
list: Do not create a new route simply because the transaction has moved to payment.
Re-check only when the nature or financial conditions materially change.
The role path below is inherited from the PO module.
The CCM or the CCM's substitute approves the payment physically or electronically.
The ACCM records the CCM approval in the commitment file before the file is submitted to the Treasurer for payment.

paySteps.text: Submit a complete and traceable payment file through the applicable Finance route.
list: Signed Payment Request included.
Invoice and contractual evidence included.
Required supporting evidence included.

paySteps.text: Retain the payment evidence through the correct accounting/file route and follow up any queries until settlement.
list: Keep the signed request and supporting evidence traceable.
Retain corrections/clarifications if Finance requests them.
Close only when the payment trail is complete.

support: Include signed contractual documents and amendments.
Fiche PO & PO Request (signed PDF format)
Consultant report / event photo / other evidence as applicable.
Fiche PO & PO Request (signed PDF format)
Accommodation, transfer, travel, signature list, agenda, event photo, etc.
Fiche PO & PO Request (signed PDF format)
Fiche PO & PO Request (signed PDF format)

Evidence that the contracted work has been completed.

payBestPractice: Confirm the service/deliverable is complete and accepted before preparing payment.
Submitting a Payment Request before confirming delivery or completion.
Match the invoice to the PO, contract/Order Form/AoE and approved amendments.
Paying against documents that do not match the approved contractual basis.
Check supplier name, amount, currency and invoice reference carefully.
Sending an invoice with inconsistent supplier or financial details.
Use the same service/expenditure route established at PO stage.
Creating a different visa route at payment stage without a reason.
Include the signed PO Request/Fiche PO and contractual documents required by the service package.
Submitting only the invoice and Payment Request.
Keep evidence of completed work in the file.
Paying without consultant deliverables, translated documents, event evidence or proof of works.
For Event Management, retain final budget, material financial-change approvals and exchange-rate evidence where required.
Ignoring changes between the initial and final event budget.
Use the most recent official Payment Request template.
Using an outdated or locally modified payment form.
Resolve discrepancies before Finance submission.
Forwarding unresolved inconsistencies and expecting Finance to reconstruct the file.
Archive Finance clarifications and final payment evidence.
Treating payment as closed once the file is submitted.
Use a Certificate of Acceptance of Work for consultants, or a Payment Request Memorandum for other expenditure, signed by the staff member who attended or received the delivery.
Submitting a payment file without a signed acceptance document.
Complete the activity report (synopsis) in the PMM IT tool when certifying the work.
Leaving the PMM activity report empty after the activity has taken place.
Obtain signed participant lists before settling event expenditure, with one list for each day of the event.
Paying for a multi-day event with a single unsigned or incomplete participant list.
Take delays and low-quality work into account when paying consultants and service providers.
Paying the full fee for late or poor work without applying the agreed sanctions.
Include the approved mission report in the file before settling mission expenditure.
Settling mission costs without a mission report that shows the link to the project.

items: Check which 2026 POs are still open and what is missing.
For completed activities, ask suppliers for invoices and supporting documents now.
Send complete payment files to Finance as soon as they are ready.
Follow up regularly for missing invoices and documents.
Check that deliverables have been accepted and the payment package is complete.
Do not keep a complete payment file until the final deadline.
Confirm all 2026 expenditure has been recorded in FIMS.
Check the Fiche PO under “Amount billed” / “Invoices”.
If everything is recorded, the PO can be finalised; there is no need to wait for the supplier payment.
Only goods delivered and services rendered by 31 December 2026 may be included in 2026 expenditure.
If delivery/performance is in 2027, use the correct 2027 treatment.
For services spanning both years, use the allocation logic shown in the “Which Financial Year?” tool below.

eoyChecklist: Review all open 2026 POs and identify what is still pending.
Ask suppliers for missing invoices and documents.
Send completed payment files to Finance as soon as possible.
Confirm goods/services included in 2026 were delivered/rendered by 31/12/2026.
Check Amount billed / Invoices before finalising each PO.
Finalise POs once all expenditure is recorded in FIMS.
Check advances, blocked invoices and other unresolved items.
Keep the final file, approvals and correspondence complete and easy to find.
auditItems: All signed contractual documents (PDF + original editable formats)
Clear and consistent file naming conventions
Evidence of service delivery (reports, signatures, photos)
Valid / correct budget lines applied throughout documentation
Written justifications for exceptions or deviations
Project documentation, including deliverables, reports, photos and visibility items, kept electronically and physically for ten years after the end of the project.
A sample of visibility items kept in the office archives, with photos of large items such as banners.
Signed participant lists for each event day, or other attendance evidence such as a group photo.
Approved mission reports kept as part of the project documentation.

fomaPoStages.label: Preparation
fomaPoStages.summary: Prepares the PO request and complete supporting file.
fomaPoStages.lead: Confirms the operational need, supplier, amount, currency, budget coding and supporting documents before submitting the file to ACCM.
fomaPoStages.action: Prepare the PO Request and assemble the complete supporting file.
fomaPoStages.control: Ensure the request is complete, accurate, authorised and supported by traceable evidence before it moves forward.
fomaPoStages.handover: Complete and controlled file transferred to ACCM.
fomaPoStages.evidence: PO Request, supporting documents, supplier information, budget/coding details.

fomaPoStages.label: Verification
fomaPoStages.summary: Checks completeness, coding and document consistency.
fomaPoStages.lead: Reviews the file before approval and checks that the request, budget information and supporting evidence are coherent and complete.
fomaPoStages.action: Verify completeness, financial coding, document consistency and the supporting trail.
fomaPoStages.control: Identify missing, inconsistent or unclear information before the request reaches the approving authority.
fomaPoStages.handover: Verified file submitted to CCM for approval.
fomaPoStages.evidence: PO Request, supporting file, financial coding, comments or corrections where needed.

fomaPoStages.label: Approval
fomaPoStages.lead: Reviews the verified request and provides the formal approval required for the purchase order process to continue.
fomaPoStages.action: Review the purpose, amount and supporting file and provide traceable approval.
fomaPoStages.control: Confirm that the expenditure is authorised and that the decision can be evidenced in the file.
fomaPoStages.handover: Approved PO request returned to ACCM for PO creation.
fomaPoStages.evidence: CCM approval and the final verified PO package.

fomaPoStages.label: PO Creation
fomaPoStages.summary: Creates the purchase order in the financial system.
fomaPoStages.lead: Uses the approved request to create the purchase order and completes the required financial-system processing.
fomaPoStages.action: Create the PO using the approved request and verified financial data.
fomaPoStages.control: Ensure the PO reflects the approved supplier, amount, currency, coding and supporting documentation.
fomaPoStages.handover: Issued PO and related information transferred to the Project Assistant.
fomaPoStages.evidence: Issued PO / Fiche PO and the approved supporting file.

fomaPoStages.label: Receipt & Follow-up
fomaPoStages.summary: Receives, checks and files the issued PO.
fomaPoStages.lead: Receives the issued purchase order, checks that it matches the request and keeps the operational file ready for the next contractual or implementation step.
fomaPoStages.action: Check the issued PO, file it with the supporting package and continue the operational follow-up.
fomaPoStages.control: Maintain continuity between the approved request, issued PO, contractual documents and later payment evidence.
fomaPoStages.handover: PO file ready for implementation and later payment follow-up.
fomaPoStages.evidence: Issued PO, final PO request package and relevant contractual/supporting documents.

fomaPaymentStages.label: Preparation
fomaPaymentStages.summary: Prepares the payment request and supporting evidence.
fomaPaymentStages.lead: Confirms that the service or deliverable is complete, prepares the Payment Request and assembles the supporting file before sending it to ACCM.
fomaPaymentStages.action: Prepare the Payment Request and complete the supporting payment file.
fomaPaymentStages.control: Make sure the request is complete, accurate and clearly linked to the relevant PO, contract, invoice and delivery evidence.
fomaPaymentStages.handover: Complete payment package transferred to ACCM for verification.
fomaPaymentStages.evidence: Payment Request, invoice, signed contractual evidence, Fiche PO / PO Request and service-specific supporting documents.

fomaPaymentStages.label: Verification
fomaPaymentStages.summary: Checks completeness and consistency of the payment file.
fomaPaymentStages.lead: Reviews the payment package before approval and checks that the request, invoice, contractual documents and delivery evidence are consistent.
fomaPaymentStages.action: Verify completeness, coding, invoice details and supporting evidence.
fomaPaymentStages.control: Detect missing documents, inconsistencies or unclear evidence before the file reaches the approving authority.
fomaPaymentStages.handover: Verified payment request submitted for CCM approval via Signaturit.
fomaPaymentStages.evidence: Verified Payment Request, invoice, contractual documents and supporting evidence.

fomaPaymentStages.label: Approval
fomaPaymentStages.lead: Reviews the verified payment request and gives the formal approval required before the file can continue to Finance processing.
fomaPaymentStages.action: Review the payment package and approve the request through Signaturit.
fomaPaymentStages.control: Confirm that the payment is authorised, supported by evidence and traceable to the underlying commitment.
fomaPaymentStages.handover: Approved request returned to ACCM for processing handover.
fomaPaymentStages.evidence: CCM approval in Signaturit and the final verified payment package.

fomaPaymentStages.label: Reception
fomaPaymentStages.summary: Receives the approved request and completes the processing handover.
fomaPaymentStages.lead: Receives the approved file, checks that the approval is visible and prepares the complete package for Finance submission.
fomaPaymentStages.action: Confirm approval, finalise the package and submit it through the applicable workflow.
fomaPaymentStages.control: Ensure the file sent to Finance is the same complete and approved file that passed verification.
fomaPaymentStages.handover: Approved payment file submitted to TPA via Workflow.
fomaPaymentStages.evidence: Approved Payment Request, invoice, contractual trail, supporting evidence and visible approval.

fomaPaymentStages.label: Payment Processing
fomaPaymentStages.summary: Receives the request through Workflow for payment processing.
fomaPaymentStages.lead: The Treasury, Payments and Accounting route receives the approved payment request and processes it through the applicable financial workflow.
fomaPaymentStages.action: Process the payment request through the Finance workflow and complete the applicable accounting controls.
fomaPaymentStages.control: Maintain a complete, consistent and traceable payment record through final processing.
fomaPaymentStages.handover: Payment request processed through the applicable Finance route.
fomaPaymentStages.evidence: Workflow record, approved payment package and associated accounting/payment evidence.

Mission Order.title: Mission Order Process Flow
Mission Order.desc: Follow the mission order from preparation through verification, pre-validation, creation and final validation.
stages: Provide mission purpose, traveller, dates, destination, cost estimates and required supporting information.

The mission must be operationally justified, sufficiently documented and authorised in advance by the Commitments Officer or the relevant CCM; the mission order is then created in the GDD travel management system.
Submit the mission order request to ACCM.
Checks the mission order request and supporting data.
Verify completeness, coding, dates, estimated costs and supporting information.
Confirm the request is complete and internally consistent.
Forward the verified request for pre-validation.
Performs pre-validation of the mission order.
Review and pre-validate the mission request in line with the applicable internal route.
Ensure the mission is properly authorised before creation; once created in GDD, the mission order is referred to the CCM for authorisation.
Return the validated request to ACCM.
Creates the mission order in the system.
Create the mission order using the verified and pre-validated information.
System data must match the approved request.
Send the created mission order for final validation.
Completes final validation of the mission order.
Perform final validation and confirm the mission order is ready for use.
No mission order should proceed with unresolved inconsistencies.
Validated mission order available for the mission process.

Expense Claim.title: Expense Claim Process Flow
Expense Claim.desc: The expense claim moves from the requester to ACCM verification and then to CCM for validation.
stages: Prepares and submits the expense claim.
Declare eligible mission expenses, attach receipts and supporting documents, and reference the approved mission order.
Claimed costs must be accurate, supported and linked to the authorised mission; the official-journey report is due within eight days of return and the reimbursement claim within fifteen days.
Submit the expense claim to ACCM.
Verifies the expense claim and evidence.
Check receipts, claimed amounts, supporting evidence and consistency with the mission order.
Only complete and supported expenditure should move forward.
Forward the verified claim for validation.
Provides formal validation of the expense claim.
Review the verified claim and complete the applicable validation.
Ensure the final claim is authorised and traceable.
Validated expense claim proceeds to the applicable payment route.

Financial Reports.title: Financial Reporting Workspace
Financial Reports.desc: Prepare and reconcile financial data, retain evidence by Budget Head and support CCM validation. Quarterly reporting is required; at least once per year the report should include actual and forecast expenditure for the coming year.
stages: Confirm VC/JP, interim/final period, contractual deadline and reporting currency.
Define the reporting scope and period.
Obtain dated FIMS/WebFOCUS extracts using the correct project and Budget Head filters.
Use dated and traceable source data.
Match spent, committed and available balances; investigate every discrepancy.
Reconcile spent, committed and available amounts.
Formulas and totals must remain consistent.
Use the correct VC/JP layout, title block, subtotals, print area and certification fields.
Presentation must not alter underlying figures.
Obtain CCM validation, transmit the clean version and archive the full audit trail.
Keep the final report and supporting evidence traceable.

Forecast.title: Forecast & Budget Revision Workflow
Forecast.desc: Use this process for reallocations, new budget lines, total-cost changes, implementation extensions or changes in project scope. Forecasts are normally prepared during annual reporting, after inception or when significant changes occur.
stages: Prepare and save the current report under the relevant Budget Head.
A traceable source workbook for the forecast.
Duplicate the report sheet, rename it FORECAST and highlight the tab in yellow.
Create a controlled forecast working sheet.
Align the number of lines and subtotal structure; extend formulas correctly.
Paste template columns after spent and committed while preserving formulas and formatting.
Use fiche staff, remaining units and contract dates to plan staff expenditure.
Reconcile charging-back units and rates by year, then calculate remaining planned units.
Hide control columns, send the working file with the RFO copied and request yellow-cell input.
Unhide columns, verify formulas and resolve inconsistencies.
No broken formulas or unexplained changes.
Create clean Variation and Budget Proposal sheets without external links.
Obtain RFO validation and return the controlled donor version to the project team.

Addendum.title: Addendum Decision Support
Addendum.desc: Start from the latest financial report and forecast. The route depends on the funding instrument, variation between subtotals and whether the donor-approved contractual budget is changing.

forecastProcess.title: Prepare the forecast working file
forecastProcess.lead: Create a complete and controlled working file before requesting Project Team input.
items: Draft an up-to-date financial report.
Create a copy of the report sheet and rename it FORECAST.
Open and adapt the appropriate JP / VC template.
Insert the calculated forecast columns after Spent and Committed.
Forecast staff expenditure using Fiche Staff and current staffing assumptions.
Calculate and reconcile charging-back lines 4.2 and 4.4.
forecastProcess.note: Keep the original financial report unchanged. Use the FORECAST sheet as the controlled working area.

forecastProcess.title: Complete the project input
forecastProcess.lead: Provide the operational assumptions needed to complete the forecast.
items: Review the working file sent by ACCM.
Complete planned expenditure for activities in the yellow cells.
Confirm the proposed staff lines, especially HQ staff.
Return the working file to ACCM for control and donor-version preparation.
forecastProcess.note: The working file is sent to the Project Team with the RFO in Cc. It should return to ACCM before any donor-facing version is prepared.

forecastProcess.title: Review input and determine the route
forecastProcess.lead: Control the returned file and identify the applicable budget-revision route.
items: Unhide the controlled columns.
Check that formulas have not been overwritten.
Review consistency of Project Team input and staffing assumptions.
For Joint Programmes, assess variation at each relevant Budget Heading.
Confirm whether the revised JP budget follows the Notification or Addendum route.
forecastProcess.note: For Joint Programmes, the route is determined at Budget Heading / subtotal level rather than against the overall project total.

forecastProcess.title: Prepare the donor version
forecastProcess.lead: Convert the controlled working file into a clean donor-facing package.
items: Copy the FORECAST sheet to a new file.
Replace working-file linked values where necessary while keeping subtotal SUM formulas.
Create the Variation sheet with amount and percentage changes.
Add the justification column for Joint Programmes.
Create the Budget Proposal sheet.
Apply the correct revised-budget / Notification / Addendum naming.
forecastProcess.note: The clean donor version should not retain uncontrolled links to the working workbook.

forecastProcess.title: Validate the package
forecastProcess.lead: Validate the financial consistency of the clean package and the selected route.
items: Review the clean donor-facing version.
Confirm the financial consistency of the revised budget.
Confirm the applicable JP / VC route.
Validate the package or return comments for correction.
forecastProcess.note: If corrections change the financial impact, reassess the route before continuing.

forecastProcess.title: Complete the CCM check
forecastProcess.lead: Complete the internal control before the file is handed back for formal submission.
items: Review the RFO-validated package for completeness and consistency.
Confirm that revised figures and supporting explanations align.
Clear the package for Project Team handover or return it for correction.
forecastProcess.note: Any correction should remain consistent across the revised budget, Variation and Budget Proposal sheets.

forecastProcess.title: Receive the cleared donor package
forecastProcess.lead: Take over the validated version and prepare the formal DPC submission.
items: Receive the cleared donor-facing package.
Confirm that the explanatory / supporting documentation is complete.
Keep the RFO in Cc when sending the file.
Forward the package through the appropriate DPC route.
docs: Explanatory note for VC, where applicable
forecastProcess.note: The validated clean version, not the internal working file, is used for the DPC submission.

forecastProcess.title: Complete the applicable DPC route
forecastProcess.lead: Process the revised budget through the DPC channel that corresponds to the funding instrument and route.
items: For Joint Programmes, the Project Team forwards to Programming + JP Unit.
For Voluntary Contributions, the Project Team forwards to Programming + RMDR.
Apply the applicable donor / EU acceptance route where required.
Retain the final confirmation or acceptance evidence.
docs: Donor / EU acceptance evidence, where applicable
forecastProcess.note: JP Notification does not require EU acceptance; JP Addendum requires EU acceptance and contractual amendment. VC donor acceptance depends on the funding arrangement.

forecastTriggers.title: Reallocation between lines or subtotals
forecastTriggers.summary: Use Forecast & Budget Revision to show the proposed movement and assess the resulting Budget Heading / subtotal variation.
checks: Identify the lines and relevant Budget Headings affected by the movement.
Show the revised distribution clearly in the working forecast.
Review the resulting variation at each relevant Budget Heading / subtotal.
Document the operational reason for the proposed reallocation.

forecastTriggers.title: Introduction of a new budget line
forecastTriggers.summary: Introduce the new cost item under the appropriate Budget Heading, then assess the resulting Budget Heading / subtotal variation. Within ±25% follows Notification; above ±25% follows Addendum.
checks: Define the new budget line and place it under the appropriate Budget Heading.
Align the revised structure while preserving formulas and subtotal calculations.
Explain why the new line is required for implementation.
Assess the resulting Budget Heading / subtotal variation and whether the new line changes the approved implementation scope.

forecastTriggers.title: Change in the project total cost
forecastTriggers.summary: A change in the overall project cost follows the Addendum route because it changes the approved contractual financial framework.
checks: Identify the amount and reason for the proposed total-cost change.
Reflect the revised total consistently across the working forecast and budget proposal.
Document the operational and financial basis for the change.
Prepare the revised package and proceed through the Addendum route.

forecastTriggers.title: Extension of the implementation period
forecastTriggers.summary: A change to the implementation period follows the Addendum route because the contractual implementation period is being amended.
checks: Confirm the proposed revised implementation period.
Reforecast staff, local-office and activity costs affected by the extension.
Reflect the extension consistently in the revised budget and supporting documents.
Prepare the extension justification and proceed through the Addendum route.

forecastTriggers.title: Change in project scope, purpose or objectives
forecastTriggers.summary: A change to the project scope, purpose or objectives affects the contractual substance and follows the Addendum route.
checks: Describe the proposed change in scope, purpose or objectives.
Identify the activities, budget lines and Budget Headings affected.
Reflect the financial effect consistently in the revised budget.
Prepare the operational justification and proceed through the Addendum route.

reportIntro.title: Why prepare a financial report?
reportIntro.text: To establish a clear and traceable picture of the project's current financial position. It shows the expenditure recorded for the reporting period and provides the controlled financial basis for review and validation.

reportIntro.title: When should it be prepared?
reportIntro.text: Prepare or update the financial report when a reporting package is required for the project. If future expenditure also needs to be planned or the budget needs to be revised, complete the current financial report first and then continue to Forecast & Budget Revision.

reportIntro.title: How is it prepared?
reportIntro.text: Build the report from the correct project and financial data, reconcile the figures, apply the appropriate JP or VC reporting structure, complete the required controls and retain the validated reporting package.

reportProcess.title: Prepare the financial report
reportProcess.lead: Establish the current financial position before any reconciliation or forward-looking exercise.
reportProcess.action: Use the correct project, Budget Head, reporting period and source figures to build the current report.
reportProcess.control: Confirm the reporting period, project references and opening structure before working on the figures.
reportProcess.output: A current financial report that can be reconciled and, if needed later, used as the baseline for Forecast & Budget Revision.

reportProcess.title: Reconcile the financial position
reportProcess.lead: Make sure the report agrees with the available financial source data.
reportProcess.action: Compare spent, committed and available balances and investigate differences rather than carrying them forward.
reportProcess.control: Check totals, commitments and unexplained differences; keep the reconciliation trace visible.
reportProcess.output: A reconciled financial position with differences resolved or clearly explained.

reportProcess.title: Apply the reporting structure
reportProcess.lead: Present the reconciled figures in the correct JP or VC reporting format.
reportProcess.action: Apply the correct layout, project references, Budget Head structure, formulas and presentation rules.
reportProcess.control: Preserve formulas and subtotals and make sure the reporting structure matches the applicable funding instrument.
reportProcess.output: A consistently structured JP / VC reporting package ready for control.

reportProcess.title: Complete the reporting controls
reportProcess.lead: Check the financial package before it is treated as a controlled version.
reportProcess.action: Review financial consistency, supporting evidence, formulas, documentary references and the audit trail.
reportProcess.control: No unexplained discrepancy, broken formula or unsupported figure should remain before finalisation.
reportProcess.output: A controlled reporting package with a clear validation trail.

reportProcess.title: Finalise and retain the report
reportProcess.lead: Close the reporting cycle and keep the version that supports subsequent review or planning.
reportProcess.action: Retain the final controlled report together with the relevant validation and supporting evidence.
reportProcess.control: Make sure the retained version is identifiable, complete and traceable to its supporting records.
reportProcess.output: The controlled financial report. If future expenditure or a budget revision is needed, continue from this baseline into Forecast & Budget Revision.

reportChecks: VC/JP, Interim/Final, reporting period and contractual reference confirmed.
Keep the FIMS/WebFOCUS extract used to prepare and reconcile the report with the working file.
Latest validated budget used: PMM document section for AP-level funding; latest amended contractual budget for specific donors.
Spent and committed figures reconcile to source data.
Subtotal formulas remain intact and differences are explained.
Budgeted lines with no expenditure are shown as 0 where required, rather than left ambiguous.
Project Team input, ACCM control, RFO validation, CCM check, Project Team handover and the applicable DPC final route are evidenced and traceable.
Report, extracts, approvals, clarifications and final clean version are archived together.

addendumReasons.title: Reallocation between budget lines or Budget Headings
addendumReasons.summary: Use this when planned expenditure needs to move within the approved budget structure.
checks: Identify the budget lines and Budget Headings affected by the reallocation.
Show the revised distribution clearly across the affected Budget Headings and budget lines.
Calculate the resulting variation at each relevant Budget Heading.
Document the operational reason for the proposed movement.

decision.title: Assess the resulting Budget Heading variation
decision.text: The reallocation itself does not automatically determine the route. For a Joint Programme, assess the resulting variation at each relevant Budget Heading.

addendumReasons.title: Introduction of new budget lines
addendumReasons.summary: Use this when implementation requires a budget line that is not currently reflected in the approved budget structure.
checks: Define the new budget line clearly and place it under the appropriate Budget Heading.
Adapt the revised budget structure and preserve the approved Budget Heading logic and subtotals.
Explain why the new line is required for implementation.
Recalculate the resulting variation at Budget Heading level.

decision.title: Assess the financial effect of the new line
decision.text: Creating a new budget line is a reason to revise the budget, but it does not by itself determine the route. For a Joint Programme, assess the resulting variation at each relevant Budget Heading.

addendumReasons.title: Change in total project cost
addendumReasons.summary: Use this when the revised financial needs change the overall cost reflected in the project budget.
checks: Identify the amount and reason for the change in total cost.
Update the revised budget consistently and reconcile the new project total.
Ensure the revised figures and supporting explanation align.
Confirm the appropriate contractual and donor route before final submission.

decision.title: Review both the budget impact and the approval route
decision.text: A change in total project cost may have broader contractual implications. For a Joint Programme, the budget route is still assessed at Budget Heading level rather than against the overall project total.

addendumReasons.title: Extension of implementation period
addendumReasons.summary: Use this when the implementation period changes and the forecast must be extended accordingly.
checks: Reflect the revised implementation period in the budget assumptions.
Review planned staff expenditure for the extended period.
Review local office and other time-dependent costs where applicable.
Confirm the revised needs with the Project Team before preparing the clean version.

decision.title: Assess the extended period before confirming the route
decision.text: An extension may change staff, local-office and activity costs. Reflect those changes first, then determine the applicable budget and approval route from the revised package.

addendumReasons.title: Change in scope, purpose or objectives
addendumReasons.summary: Use this when changes to implementation affect what the project is expected to deliver or achieve.
checks: Describe the proposed change and its operational impact.
Identify the budget lines and Budget Headings affected.
Reflect the financial impact consistently in the revised budget package.
Ensure the Project Team provides the necessary justification before submission.

decision.title: Confirm the wider approval implications
decision.text: Changes to scope, purpose or objectives may affect more than the budget. Make the financial impact clear in the revised package and confirm the applicable approval route before submission.

addendumSteps.title: Confirm the Addendum route
addendumSteps.lead: Confirm that the Joint Programme revision follows the Addendum route before preparing the package.
items: Review the proposed budget revision and confirm the figures are consistent.
Assess variation at the level of each relevant Budget Heading.
Where any relevant Budget Heading exceeds ±25%, apply the Addendum route.
Check PMM → Documents → Contract to identify the next Addendum number.
addendumSteps.note: The ±25% threshold is assessed at Budget Heading / subtotal level, not against the overall project total.

addendumSteps.title: Prepare the revised budget
addendumSteps.lead: Prepare the controlled revised-budget proposal for the Addendum package.
items: Use the validated revision figures as the basis for the revised budget.
Apply the title “Budget for all Years – Addendum n°…” using the correct sequence.
Confirm formulas and subtotal calculations remain intact.
Ensure the revised figures reflect the agreed Project Team input.
addendumSteps.note: Keep internal working calculations separate from the donor-facing package.

addendumSteps.title: Complete the justification
addendumSteps.lead: Provide the operational explanation supporting the proposed budget movements.
items: Review the proposed revised budget.
Complete the justification for the relevant variations.
Confirm the proposed activity and staff assumptions where applicable.
Return the completed input for preparation of the donor package.
addendumSteps.note: For Joint Programmes, the Variation sheet includes a justification column.

addendumSteps.title: Prepare the donor package
addendumSteps.lead: Create a clean package that can move through validation and submission.
items: Create a clean donor-facing file from the validated revised budget.
Replace working-file linked values where required while preserving subtotal SUM formulas.
Create the Variation sheet showing variation in amount and percentage.
Include the JP justification column.
Create the Budget Proposal sheet.
Name the file with the JP reference and applicable Addendum number.
addendumSteps.note: The clean donor version should not retain uncontrolled links to the working file.

addendumSteps.title: Validate the package
addendumSteps.lead: Validate the revised budget package before it moves to the next control point.
items: Review the financial consistency of the revised budget.
Confirm the Addendum route and supporting budget analysis.
Check that the donor-facing package is complete.
Validate the package or return comments for correction.
addendumSteps.note: If corrections affect the Budget Heading variation, reconfirm the route before continuing.

addendumSteps.title: Complete the CCM check
addendumSteps.lead: Complete the internal check before the package is handed back for formal submission.
items: Check the validated package for completeness and consistency.
Confirm that the revised budget and supporting explanation align.
Clear the package for Project Team handover or return it for correction.
addendumSteps.note: Corrections should be reflected consistently across the revised budget, Variation and Budget Proposal sheets.

addendumSteps.title: Submit the package to DPC
addendumSteps.lead: Forward the cleared Joint Programme package through the appropriate DPC route.
items: Receive the cleared donor package.
Forward the package to DPC Programming + JP Unit.
Include the completed justification and the supporting documentation.
Keep the RFO in Cc when sending the file.
addendumSteps.note: The donor-facing package should contain only the cleared, controlled version.

addendumSteps.title: EU acceptance and contractual signature
addendumSteps.lead: Complete the external acceptance and contractual amendment route.
items: The Addendum route requires EU acceptance.
The contractual amendment is signed by the EU and the Council of Europe DSG.
Retain the final acceptance and signed amendment as part of the project record.
addendumSteps.note: The revised budget is uploaded to PMM only after the amendment has been signed by both parties.

addendumSteps.title: Update project records
addendumSteps.lead: Close the process by aligning the operational records with the signed Addendum.
items: Upload the revised budget to PMM after signature by both parties.
Revise the Delegation Letter to the office.
Update the Fiche Staff.
Retain the signed amendment and final supporting package in the project file.
addendumSteps.note: The signed Addendum becomes the basis for the updated project budget records.

addendumKeys: Confirm the change first, then apply the Addendum route only to the affected elements.
Keep the revised figures consistent across every affected Budget Heading and supporting calculation.
The justification should explain the operational reason for the change, not repeat the financial figures.
The donor package must be clean, controlled and free from uncontrolled working-file links.
Any correction made during validation must be reflected consistently throughout the package.
CCM clearance should be based on the RFO-validated version.
Send the cleared package to the Project Team for onward submission to DPC; keep the RFO in Cc.
The revised budget is uploaded to PMM only after the amendment is signed by both parties.
Close the process only when the signed Addendum and all related project records are aligned.

Foundations: Confirm procurement—not a grant—is the correct instrument.
Confirm no known conflict of interest.
Apply equal treatment and transparency from the start.
Contract Types: Need pattern is classified: one-off / recurrent defined units / variable uncertain.
Contract type is not being confused with procedure type.
Framework duration and ordering method are defined where relevant.
No overlap with an existing framework contract/agreement.
Need & Planning: Similar foreseeable needs have been consolidated.
Existing contracts/database checked before launching a new tender.
Market analysis and supplier sourcing are proportionate to the need.
Reverse schedule includes approvals, publication, VAT and delivery.
Thresholds & Procedure: Total intended duration and renewals included.
Value assessed over the correct period of reference.
No artificial splitting or per-supplier calculation.
Funding source identified for validation route.
Tender Design: Exclusion, eligibility and award criteria defined before publication.
Eligibility criteria are measurable and proportionate.
Award criteria and weights are clear.
Submission, contractual and delivery conditions are complete.
Launch & Publication: At least three suppliers invited where competitive bidding is not published, or exception recorded.
Publication channel and deadline are documented.
E-procurement requirement checked for the current date/value.
Evaluation: At least two authorised staff analyse the tender as required by the guide.
Award scoring uses only published criteria with written reasons.
Clarification & Negotiation: All exchanges are written and retained.
Negotiation approval obtained from CCM/TB where required.
Negotiations do not significantly change tender specifications.
Final changes are confirmed by bidders in writing.
Award: Recommendation traces back to evaluation evidence.
Contract is concluded before unsuccessful bidders are notified.
Unsuccessful bidder notifications include reason and enquiry route.
Contract Signing: AoE/contract complete and signed by supplier.
PO/budgetary commitment created before Council signature.
No performance starts before Council signature.
Final signed documents sent and archived.
Contract Management: Delivery deadline and contract end date tracked separately.
Framework expenditure monitored against original threshold.
Supplier performance documented during and at end of contract.
Breach/termination steps documented and escalated where needed.
Contract Execution & Payment: VAT status and place of taxation clarified before signature.
Bank account matches contractual payment details.
Payment terms and any schedule reflected in contract.
Payment evidence is filed through the correct route.
Filing & Audit Trail: Tender documents and all bids archived.
Execution evidence retained by buyer entity.
Performance learning captured for future procurement.

procurementBestPractice.Need & Planning: Check the shared contract database and market before launching a new procedure. Use long-term planning to reduce repeated procurement effort.
procurementBestPractice.Thresholds & Procedure: If the estimate is close to €184,000, use the international route rather than risk exceeding the threshold later.
procurementBestPractice.Tender Design: Download a fresh template at the start of each procurement process because templates are updated over time.
procurementBestPractice.Launch & Publication: Publish at a sensible time and give suppliers a deadline proportionate to the complexity of the tender.
procurementBestPractice.Evaluation: Write clear, exhaustive reasons for technical/quality scores; strong documentation makes later enquiries and audits easier.
procurementBestPractice.Contract Management: Use reminders and proactive supplier communication before deadlines rather than reacting after a missed delivery date.
procurementBestPractice.Filing & Audit Trail: Archive as the process runs, not at the end. This preserves a cleaner and more reliable audit trail.

buyer.name: Buyer entity / project team
buyer.summary: The Council of Europe entity for which the purchase is made. It runs the process from forecasting the need to executing the contract.
does: Defines needs and estimates the threshold
Prepares tender documents and technical specifications
Invites or publishes and answers questions
Submits files to the CCM or Tenders Board
Receives and accepts deliverables and verifies invoices
Monitors contract execution and supplier performance

authorised.name: Authorised staff members
authorised.summary: Members of the buyer entity authorised in writing by the CO or CCM (Rule No. 1395, Article 3.2.d) to perform key procedure tasks.
authorised.when: From approval of the tender documents until the award.
does: Open offers or represent the buyer entity at opening
Assess offers, with at least two assessors
Conduct negotiations with tenderers when authorised
Report indications of fraud or collusion

ccm.name: Commitments Officer / Cost Centre Manager
ccm.summary: COs authorise expenditure and delegate to CCMs. The CCM is responsible for the cost centre's purchases and decides on competitive bidding procedures and direct awards below €184,000.
ccm.when: At every validation and signature point.
does: Validates the choice of procedure and the tender documents
Authorises launch, deadline extensions and negotiations
Decides awards for competitive bidding procedures
Approves direct awards below €184,000
Signs contracts, orders and call-offs
Decides consequences of missed deadlines and approves amendments

tb.name: Tenders Board
tb.summary: Ensures compliance with the rules for all contracts above €184,000 excluding VAT. It is chaired by the Director General of Administration, with the DLAPIL Director, the Treasurer and an MAE member.
tb.when: For international public calls, direct awards from €184,000, call-offs above €184,000 and complaints.
does: Authorises the launch and publication of international calls
Scrutinises bid analyses and decides on awards
Authorises negotiations, amendments and direct awards
Decides on unfruitful or discontinued international calls
Rules on complaints within 30 days

tbsec.name: Secretariat of the Tenders Board
tbsec.summary: Part of the DGA's Legal Support Division. It runs the Tenders Board's calendar, templates, SharePoint and consultations, and checks files before submission.
tbsec.when: Before and during Tenders Board procedures.
does: Reviews files before they go to the Board
Runs electronic consultations with at least 48 hours for members
Publishes international calls after approval
Opens bids at cdm@coe.int when e-procurement is not used
Archives Tenders Board decisions

dlapil.name: DLAPIL
dlapil.summary: The Directorate of Legal Advice and Public International Law handles all legal procurement questions and templates. It performs the Legal Compliance Review for extrabudgetary-funded procedures from €55,000 to €184,000.
dlapil.when: For any legal question, and mandatorily for Legal Compliance Reviews.
does: Provides tender file, act of engagement and order form templates
Carries out the Legal Compliance Review within 5 working days
Advises on legal conditions, amendments and breaches
Provides third-party purchase templates on request
Trains staff on procurement procedures

pu.name: Procurement Unit (DGA)
pu.summary: Manages all DGA purchases and advises every buyer entity on non-legal procurement issues and tools, including e-procurement. It responds within a 48-hour SLA.
pu.when: From market analysis to contract execution.
does: Supports market analysis, sourcing and calls for expressions of interest
Maintains the suppliers and contracts databases
Supports e-procurement and OJEU publication
Provides analysis tables and expenditure tracking tools
Monitors procurement KPIs and purchase mapping

tpa.name: Treasury, Payments and Accounting (TPA)
tpa.summary: Registers suppliers and bank details in FIMS, checks payment claims and pays suppliers.
tpa.when: At supplier registration and at payment.
does: Processes MSA 4002 supplier creation in FIMS
Checks payment claims and settles invoices
Approves specific payment conditions
Provides card numbers for exceptional card payments
Keeps invoices and payment requests

dpc.name: Directorate of Programme Co-ordination (DPC)
dpc.summary: Co-ordinates programming and resource mobilisation for extrabudgetary co-operation projects and ensures they comply with the project management methodology.
does: Advises on existing framework contracts in external offices
Addresses donor visibility and communication requirements
Gives guidance on hiring civil servants from Horizontal Facility beneficiaries
Ensures activities match the approved project budget

dio.name: Directorate of Internal Oversight (DIO)
dio.summary: Provides independent audit, evaluation and investigation, including compliance and performance audits of procurement.
dio.when: When audits take place or wrongdoing is suspected.
does: Audits procurement compliance and performance
Receives reports of fraud, corruption and wrongdoing
Investigates suspected proscribed practices
Reports on risks detected in declarations of interests

Foundations: Confirm grant is the correct instrument.
Identify funding source and donor conditions.
Costs: Each cost is necessary and budgeted.

grantBestPractice.Principles: Define co-financing, implementation timing and non-cumulative funding logic before publication; these are harder to correct later.
grantBestPractice.Criteria: Test every criterion before publication: Is it objective, proportionate, relevant and verifiable? Can the supporting document actually prove it?
grantBestPractice.Call & Publication: Use the call-content checklist and obtain legal input before publication where the draft includes special conditions or sensitive submission arrangements.
grantBestPractice.Evaluation: Separate the gates clearly: exclusion → eligibility → award. Keep reasoning and evidence at each stage so the final decision is traceable.
grantBestPractice.Agreement: Set the implementation period, reporting and payment architecture precisely before signature; later amendments cannot be used to redesign the award.
grantBestPractice.Filing: Archive progressively throughout the procedure rather than reconstructing the file at close-out.

staff: If necessary for implementation, incurred in the implementation period, identifiable/verifiable, lawful, evidenced and included in the estimated budget.
travel: Apply the same direct-cost test: necessity, cost-effectiveness, implementation period, evidence and approved budget.
equipment: Must be necessary for the action/project and satisfy the full direct eligible-cost test.
indirect: Indirect eligible costs must be specified in the call/agreement and cannot exceed 7% of the total.
renovation: Renovation costs are excluded unless directly related to the project/action and precisely specified in its description.
land: Purchase of land and buildings is explicitly excluded.
fx: Currency exchange losses are explicitly ineligible.
other: Ask: Is it necessary? cost-effective? incurred during implementation? identifiable/verifiable? compliant with tax/social law? supported by originals/certified copies? included in the estimated budget?

one: One supplier; lots may be awarded separately.
Direct contract; no additional competition after signature.
Use for a clearly defined, quantifiable need that is unlikely to recur.
fc: Order forms; ranking or pooling where several suppliers are used.
Use for recurring needs with definable units but uncertain total volume.
fa: Call-off mini-competition for each specific need.
Use for regular but variable or complex needs where precise deliverables are not known upfront.

direct.title: Direct Award
direct.desc: A compact route for a clearly defined low-value need. Keep the decision proportionate, but leave a complete and traceable procurement file.
steps: Confirm scope, estimated full value, purchase type and available budget.
Record the supplier/price choice and value-for-money basis; keep the supporting evidence.
Create the required PO / budgetary commitment before contractual signature where applicable.
Obtain the applicable CCM validation before final commitment.
Use the appropriate contractual document and ensure it is in place before work starts.
Keep the procurement, approval, contract/order and financial evidence together.
docs: Clear description of what is being purchased.
Quotation, public price or other supporting price evidence.
Short justification / value-for-money record as applicable.

competitive.title: Competitive Bidding
competitive.desc: The normal route above the direct-award limit and below the international threshold. The funding source can add a legal-validation step.
steps: Confirm the whole foreseeable need, estimated value, funding source, timetable and procurement documents.
Finalise specifications, eligibility / award criteria, invitation and evaluation material.
Invite at least three potential suppliers where applicable, or use the permitted public-price comparison route when its conditions are met.
Document admissibility, exclusion / eligibility checks and award assessment using the published criteria.
For extrabudgetary or mixed funding from €55,000 to below €184,000, complete DLAPIL Legal Compliance Review before CCM approval.
Submit the complete procedure and evaluation record for CCM approval.
Complete the contract / PO route and retain the tender, evaluation, approval and signature trail.
docs: Complete supplier submissions and receipt trail.
Final contractual and financial commitment documents.

international.title: International Public Call for Tenders
international.desc: Use when the total foreseeable need reaches €184,000. Build in the longer publication, evaluation and Tenders Board route from the outset.
steps: Confirm the total foreseeable need and prepare the international-procedure timetable and procurement package.
Obtain the applicable Tenders Board authorisation for launch before publication.
Launch the international call through the required e-procurement / publication route.
Complete admissibility, exclusion, eligibility and award evaluation with a fully documented record.
Submit the evaluation outcome through the applicable Tenders Board validation / award route.
Complete the authorised contractual signature and financial commitment route.
Retain publication, bids, evaluation, Board decisions, contract and financial evidence as one audit trail.
docs: Specifications, criteria, contractual documents and publication material.
Admissibility, exclusion, eligibility and award records.
Launch and applicable award / validation evidence.
